intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos port.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, spices, cheeses, and cured meats. Sample street foods like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided food tour enhances the experience with tastings and cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the shallow waters to the small island, snorkel among sea life, and relax on one of Greece's most beautiful and unique beaches. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania to learn how to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and homemade baklava. Classes typically include a visit to a local market to source fresh ingredients, followed by a communal meal with local wine or raki.

experiences.name: Sunset Dinner at a Santorini Caldera Taverna
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset while dining at a cliffside taverna overlooking the volcanic caldera. Enjoy fresh grilled octopus, fava dip made from local yellow split peas, fresh catch of the day, and a glass of Assyrtiko white wine — a grape variety unique to Santorini. Oia and Imerovigli offer the most spectacular views.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at destination airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, take a budget bus or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea right at the hotel beach.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the nearest local village strip to scout tavernas and souvenir shops. Enjoy a slow sunset walk along the waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap or cheese pie (tiropita) from a bakery or street kiosk near the airport or bus stop – around €2–4
meals.dinner: Find a neighbourhood taverna near the resort and try a classic Greek salad (horiatiki) and grilled souvlaki – budget around €8–12 per person including a local beer

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a local SIM card at the airport for cheap data. Ask hotel staff for their favourite budget eating spots – locals always know best.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and enjoy the hotel's beachfront at its quietest. Take a long morning swim in the warm sea, then explore the immediate coastal path on foot for about an hour to discover hidden coves nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town centre on a local bus (€1–2 each way). Visit the central market (laiki agora) to browse fresh produce, olives, local honey, and spices. Pick up cheap snacks for later in the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Watch the sunset from the beach with a cold Mythos beer bought from a mini-market (€1.50). Stroll to a waterfront psarotaverna (fish taverna) for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Simple continental breakfast at the hotel or grab a koulouri sesame bread ring and a freddo espresso from a local café – €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh spanakopita (spinach pie) and a small salad from a bakery in the town market – €3–5
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus or calamari with a side of tzatziki and pita bread at a local psarotaverna – €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: The local bus is the most budget-friendly transport option. Check the timetable at the hotel reception or ask staff.

day_by_day.morning: Pack a beach bag and head to a nearby public beach (non-resort beach) accessible by local bus or a 20–30 min walk. Bring snacks from the mini-market. Swim, snorkel if you have gear, and sunbathe on quieter sands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby archaeological site or hilltop village on foot or by local bus. Take photos, visit a small local church, and enjoy panoramic views of the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Back at the resort area, find a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) and share several small plates with travel companions or enjoy solo tasting.

meals.breakfast: Greek yoghurt with local honey and walnuts from the market – eat at the hotel or a café – €3–4
meals.lunch: Pack a DIY picnic: olives, feta, bread, tomatoes, and fruit bought from the local market – €4–6 total
meals.dinner: Mezedes spread: hummus, dolmades, taramasalata, and grilled halloumi at a local mezedopoleio – €9–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy a reusable water bottle and refill it – tap water is drinkable in most Greek towns and saves money over buying plastic bottles.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or low-cost self-guided walking tour of the nearest historic old town. Look for Venetian or Ottoman architecture, old harbours, and traditional whitewashed alleyways. Most towns have free printed maps at tourist offices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a shaded café in the old town and spend an hour people-watching over a Greek coffee (ellinikos kafes – €1.50). Then visit a free local museum or gallery if available, or browse artisan shops without pressure to buy.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the harbour waterfront for the evening volta (the Greek tradition of an evening stroll). Join locals as the town comes alive after the heat of the day.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (custard or cheese-filled pastry) and a coffee at a local pastry shop – €2.50–4
meals.lunch: A simple plate of moussaka or pastitsio at a no-frills local eatery (mageirio) – €6–9
meals.dinner: Grilled chicken or pork souvlaki with pita, onions, and tzatziki from a street souvlaki stall – €3–5

day_by_day.notes: Mageirio (cook-shops) are the best budget dining secret in Greece – they serve home-style daily specials at very low prices, popular with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning at the resort's own beachfront. Arrive early to claim a good spot before it fills up. Practice snorkelling or simply float and relax in the warm Aegean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (€5–10/day from local hire shops) and cycle along coastal roads to explore the surrounding area. Stop at any inviting beach or viewpoint along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes, shower and change. Seek out a local ouzerie (ouzo bar) for the authentic Greek aperitivo experience with free small meze bites served alongside drinks.

meals.breakfast: Scrambled eggs and toast at the hotel or a café – €3–5
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside kiosk or small taverna during the bike ride for a toasted sandwich (tost) or a gyros – €2–4
meals.dinner: Baked lamb or stuffed tomatoes (gemista) at a traditional taverna – €9–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Cycling is both budget-friendly and a great way to discover spots that tour buses miss. Bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early local bus or ferry (if applicable) to a neighbouring beach or coastal village known for clearer water. Spend the morning swimming and relaxing before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the village on foot. Visit the local church, chat with fishermen at the harbour, and browse the small shops. Look for locally made products like olive oil soap, herbs, or handmade ceramics as affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in the village before heading back to the resort. Enjoy the slower pace of a smaller community.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh koulouri and a coffee to eat on the bus or ferry – €2
meals.lunch: Fresh fish of the day at a small harbour-side taverna – ask for the daily catch to get the best price – €10–15
meals.dinner: Simple village taverna meal: horta (wild greens), bread, and grilled meat – €8–11 per person

day_by_day.notes: Asking for the 'catch of the day' or 'daily special' almost always gets you the freshest and cheapest option on the menu.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Sleep in slightly, take a leisurely swim at the hotel beach, and do some journalling or reading under a beach umbrella.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove or small winery if one is accessible nearby – many offer free or very cheap tastings. Alternatively, find a shaded hilltop with a view and enjoy the landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or assemble your own dinner using market ingredients (if you have access to a kitchen or kitchenette) or treat yourself to a slightly nicer taverna meal as a midpoint-trip celebration.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the hotel or a café: eggs, olives, feta, tomatoes, bread – €4–7
meals.lunch: Self-assembled mezze platter using market buys: olives, feta, cured meats, bread, and fruit – €5–7
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly larger taverna meal: lamb chops (paidakia), Greek salad, and a carafe of house wine – €15–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is a good halfway point to review your budget spending and adjust plans for the second week if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach walk to collect sea glass or shells. Watch local fishing boats return with their catch. If possible, buy directly from fishermen for the freshest and cheapest seafood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach that requires a short hike to reach – these are almost always less crowded and more beautiful. Bring water and snacks. Swim in crystal-clear water away from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Back at the resort area, find a rooftop bar or terrace café for a sundowner drink with a view, then move to a budget dinner spot.

meals.breakfast: Honey and tahini on toast with a freddo cappuccino at a local café – €3–4
meals.lunch: Packed picnic from the mini-market: crackers, hummus, vegetables, and cheese – €4–6
meals.dinner: Chicken gyros plate with chips and tzatziki at a local grill house – €7–10 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hidden beaches accessible by foot often require a 20–45 minute hike but reward you with dramatically better scenery and fewer people.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to a larger nearby town for a half-day exploration. Visit the central square (plateia), a Byzantine church, or a Venetian fortress if one exists in the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse the town's street market or permanent shops for affordable local products. Try loukoumades (Greek honey doughnuts) from a street vendor as an afternoon snack.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in the larger town for dinner before the last bus back, or take a taxi back if buses have stopped (split the cost with other travellers if possible).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick café stop before catching the bus – €3–5
meals.lunch: Souvlaki wrap and a cold drink from a busy local grill – always a sign of good quality – €4–6
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek taverna in the town: stuffed peppers, grilled fish, and house salad – €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Loukoumades stalls are a must-try street food – look for queues of locals as a quality indicator. They cost around €3–5 for a generous portion.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach morning at one of the area's best-rated public beaches. Arrive by 09:00 to get a good spot. Bring your own towel, water, and snacks to avoid paying for sun loungers and overpriced beach bars.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a free or cheap water activity: cliff jumping at a designated safe spot (ask locals), stand-up paddleboard rental (€10–15/hour), or kayaking along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a taverna with a sea view. Order simply: a shared mezze starter, one main each, and a shared carafe of local wine.

meals.breakfast: Yoghurt parfait with granola and honey from a beachside café – €3–5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the mini-market eaten on the beach – €4–6
meals.dinner: Sea-view taverna: grilled sea bream, Greek salad, tzatziki, and house wine carafe – €12–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Renting a paddleboard or kayak is much cheaper than organised boat tours and gives you more freedom to explore the coastline at your own pace.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring a local fishing village within easy reach. Watch the daily life of fishermen mending nets, visit a small chapel perched on a rock, and take photos of colourful caïques (traditional wooden boats).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a long afternoon swim at a secluded beach near the fishing village. The water in late June is warm and ideal for extended swimming sessions. Dry off and enjoy a cold frappe in the shade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local panigiri (village festival) if one is happening – these are free, lively, and feature live music, dancing, and cheap food and drink.

meals.breakfast: Cheese pie and coffee from a village bakery – €2–3
meals.lunch: Fried calamari and chips at a harbour-side snack bar in the fishing village – €6–9
meals.dinner: If a panigiri is on, eat from the festival food stalls (souvlaki, loukoumades, grilled meats) – €5–8. Otherwise, a local taverna for grilled lamb chops – €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check with hotel staff or local tourist boards about any upcoming village festivals (panigiri) – they are one of the most authentic and budget-friendly Greek experiences you can have.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning at the beach. Swim, relax, and soak up the last of the Aegean sunshine. Take a final snorkelling session and try to spot sea urchins, small fish, and starfish in the shallows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the local village. Focus on affordable, authentic items: local honey jars (€3–5), small bottles of olive oil (€4–6), dried herbs like oregano or thyme (€2–3), or handmade ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favourite taverna discovered during the trip. Order your best-loved dishes from the week and enjoy a final Greek sunset.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast to fuel the day – eggs, feta, tomatoes, olives, bread, and coffee – €5–7
meals.lunch: One last gyros wrap or souvlaki from your favourite local grill – €3–5
meals.dinner: Favourite taverna revisited: whatever you enjoyed most during the trip, plus a dessert of galaktoboureko (custard pastry) or baklava – €12–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight to make the final morning stress-free. Leave a small tip for favourite restaurant staff – it is appreciated and not always expected in Greece.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one last sunrise swim if your flight allows. Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort, store luggage with reception if needed, and take a final walk along the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, either head directly to the airport by budget bus or shuttle, or spend a final hour at a café near the resort with a Greek coffee and pastry before departing.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with a suitcase of memories, a taste for Greek food, and a sun-kissed glow. Flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek coffee and a koulouri or tiropita at a local café near the resort – €2–4
meals.lunch: Airport meal or a packed snack from the mini-market if departing early – €4–8
meals.dinner: In-flight or at home

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Budget bus or shared shuttle to the airport is the cheapest option – book the day before if possible.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (~2-3 hours depending on location). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea for the first time.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate hotel surroundings and nearby waterfront promenade. Watch the sunset from the beach or hotel terrace with a glass of local wine or ouzo.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap or spanakopita from a local bakery or kiosk near the resort upon arrival (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby taverna — try grilled octopus, Greek salad, and fresh bread with tzatziki (~€20-28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Hydrate well after the flight. Exchange currency or withdraw euros at the airport ATM for better rates. The sea temperature in June is around 24-25°C — perfect for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and enjoy a swim at the hotel's beachfront before the crowds arrive. Walk along the shoreline for 30-45 minutes to explore the local beach scene. Collect sea glass or simply relax in the morning calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local village or town center. Browse the open-air market (laiki agora) for fresh produce, olives, honey, and local cheeses. Pop into a small local bakery for traditional loukoumades (honey doughnuts).
day_by_day.evening: Head to a seaside fish taverna for a classic Greek seafood dinner. Watch the fishing boats come in at the local harbor if accessible.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet or a nearby café — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, fresh fruit, and strong Greek coffee (~€8-12)
meals.lunch: Mezze spread at a local taverna — hummus, taramasalata, dolmades, and pita (~€12-16 per person)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish (lavraki or tsipoura) with lemon and olive oil, village salad, and a carafe of house white wine at a harbor-side taverna (~€25-32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sunscreen SPF 50+ — the June sun is intense between 11:00 and 16:00. A hat and sunglasses are essential. Most shops close for an afternoon siesta between 14:00-17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning snorkeling session at a nearby rocky cove or clear-water beach. Rent snorkeling gear from a local beach shop (~€8-12). Explore underwater rock formations and spot sea urchins, small fish, and starfish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local archaeological site or ancient ruins within day-trip distance. Many Greek coastal areas have nearby ancient temples, Byzantine churches, or Venetian fortresses. Hire a local guide or use an audio guide app for context (~€10-15 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a relaxed evening. Try a local ouzeri (ouzo bar) with small mezze plates — the authentic Greek way to socialize.

meals.breakfast: Fresh orange juice, scrambled eggs, feta cheese, and olives at a local café (~€7-10)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local deli or bakery — cheese pie (tiropita), tomato, and a cold Mythos beer eaten at the ruins or beach (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Dinner at an ouzeri — order a selection of mezze: grilled sardines, fava bean dip, fried zucchini, and saganaki (fried cheese) (~€18-24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Archaeological sites typically open at 08:00 and close at 20:00 in summer. Carry water — at least 1.5 liters per person. Comfortable walking shoes are recommended for ruins.

day_by_day.morning: Book a morning boat trip or water taxi to a nearby secluded beach or sea cave accessible only by water. Many Greek coastal resorts offer 2-3 hour morning excursions (~€25-40 per person). Swim in crystal-clear waters away from the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from boat trip. Spend the afternoon at the hotel beach — rent a sunbed and umbrella (~€8-10 for two) and read, swim, and relax. Try paddleboarding or kayaking from the beach rental shack (~€12-15/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a cliffside or rooftop bar. Try an Aperol Spritz or a classic Greek Negroni with mastiha liqueur.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with granola and fresh figs, and a freddo cappuccino at a beachside café (~€8-11)
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat or at a beach cantina — toasted sandwich (tost) with cheese and ham, or a fresh fruit platter (~€8-12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the village — lamb kleftiko (slow-cooked lamb), roasted potatoes, and horiatiki salad (~€22-28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book boat trips the evening before as they fill up quickly in peak season. Apply waterproof sunscreen before the boat excursion. The sea caves are most beautifully lit in the morning when sunlight enters from the water.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided or self-guided hiking trail along the coastal path near the resort. Many Greek coastal areas have marked trails with stunning sea views. A 2-3 hour moderate walk offers panoramic vistas and wildflower meadows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove or winery for a short tasting tour. Many small family-run estates offer informal tastings of local olive oil, wine, and honey (~€10-20 per person including tastings). Learn about traditional Greek agricultural practices.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural event if available — summer evenings often feature open-air cinema, live Greek music, or traditional dance performances in village squares.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the hotel — eggs, local sausages, feta, tomatoes, olives, and fresh bread (~€10-14)
meals.lunch: At the winery or olive grove — antipasti-style spread with local cheeses, cured meats, olives, and bread paired with wine (~€15-20 per person)
meals.dinner: Souvlaki night — visit a local souvlaki joint for pork or chicken skewers, pita, tzatziki, and fries — a true local favorite (~€10-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hiking trails can be rocky and uneven. Wear proper footwear. Start the hike before 09:30 to avoid the midday heat. Carry snacks and extra water. Check local event boards at the hotel or village square for evening entertainment.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at the hotel beach — swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the peak-summer atmosphere. Practice some Greek phrases with locals. Many beach vendors sell fresh watermelon slices and coconut — a perfect morning treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a cooking class or food workshop in the local area. Many Greek villages offer 2-3 hour hands-on sessions teaching traditional dishes like moussaka, spanakopita, or baklava (~€45-65 per person). A wonderful way to connect with local food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Use your cooking class recipes as inspiration and dine at a traditional Greek home-style restaurant (estiatorio) where daily specials are displayed in the kitchen window.

meals.breakfast: Honey toast with sesame tahini and a cold frappe coffee at a local café (~€6-9)
meals.lunch: Light lunch before the cooking class — a simple Greek salad and fresh bread (~€9-12)
meals.dinner: At a traditional estiatorio — try the daily special (mageirefta), which might include pastitsio, stuffed peppers, or bean soup with crusty bread (~€16-22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book cooking classes in advance — they are very popular in summer. Most classes include a communal meal at the end, so adjust lunch accordingly. Bring a notebook to write down recipes to recreate at home.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby island or peninsula (if applicable to your resort location). Take a ferry or water taxi for a half-day exploration. Walk through narrow whitewashed alleyways, visit a hilltop chapel, and enjoy the authentic island atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island's main beach and swim in its turquoise waters. Browse local artisan shops for handmade ceramics, leather sandals, and natural sponges — classic Greek souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner back at the hotel or a nearby taverna to rest after the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pastries, fruit, and coffee (~€8-10)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the island — grilled shrimp, calamari, and a cold Alfa beer at a harbor-side restaurant (~€20-26 per person)
meals.dinner: Light dinner back at the resort — mezze platter, fresh bread, and local rosé wine (~€16-20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules the day before and book tickets early in peak season. Carry a small daypack with sunscreen, water, a light layer, and your camera. The ferry journey itself often offers spectacular coastal views.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and take a slow swim. Read a book in the shade of a beach umbrella. This is your recharge day mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local spa or wellness center for a traditional Greek herbal treatment or massage (~€40-60 for a 60-minute session). Alternatively, explore a nearby monastery or Byzantine church for a peaceful cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a clifftop or elevated restaurant with panoramic sea views. Splurge slightly on a nicer restaurant for the midpoint of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — full spread with eggs made to order, fresh juices, and pastries (~€12-16)
meals.lunch: Light poolside or beachside snack — fruit salad, a club sandwich, and iced coffee (~€10-14)
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a scenic restaurant — grilled sea bass, orzo with lobster (astakos), or lamb chops with roasted vegetables and a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine (~€35-45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 8 is intentionally slower-paced to prevent travel fatigue. Greece's pace naturally encourages slowing down — embrace the concept of 'siga siga' (slowly, slowly). Book the sunset dinner restaurant in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a local fish market (if available) to see the daily catch. Chat with fishermen and local vendors. Purchase fresh ingredients if you have access to a kitchen, or simply enjoy the vibrant market atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach exploration — rent a scooter or bicycle (~€15-25/day) and ride along the coastal road to discover hidden beaches and coves not accessible on foot. Pack a small bag with snacks and water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to a favorite taverna discovered earlier in the trip. Revisit familiar faces and try dishes you haven't yet ordered — Greeks appreciate returning customers and often treat regulars with complimentary dessert or ouzo.

meals.breakfast: At the fish market area — freshly fried anchovies or a savory cheese pie from a market stall (~€5-8)
meals.lunch: Picnic on a hidden beach — local bread, olives, feta, tomatoes, and cold cuts purchased from a deli (~€10-14)
meals.dinner: Return to a favorite taverna — try grilled swordfish steak, gigantes beans in tomato sauce, and tiramisu or galaktoboureko (custard pastry) for dessert (~€22-28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fish markets are typically active from 06:00-10:00. Scooter rental requires a valid driving license (category AM or A in Europe). Always wear a helmet. Check the scooter's condition before renting and take photos of any existing damage.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) session on calm morning waters (~€15-20/hour rental). The sea is typically glassiest before 09:00. Alternatively, join a group yoga session on the beach if offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local museum — archaeological, maritime, or folk art — for cultural depth. Most regional Greek museums are small, manageable in 1-2 hours, and very affordable (~€4-8 entry). Air-conditioned relief from the afternoon heat is a bonus.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local nightlife scene — Greece comes alive after dark. Join locals at a beachside bar for cocktails, or find a live Greek music venue (rebetiko or laika music) for an authentic cultural evening.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-activity breakfast — a banana, Greek yogurt, and water before paddleboarding. Full breakfast after at a café (~€9-12)
meals.lunch: Museum café or a nearby sandwich shop — grilled chicken wrap with tzatziki and a fresh lemonade (~€10-13)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a lively taverna with live music — shared plates of mezze, grilled meats, and plenty of local wine (~€20-26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Greek nightlife starts late — locals rarely dine before 21:00 and bars fill up after 23:00. Embrace the late schedule for an authentic experience. Keep the following morning relaxed to recover.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning after the late night. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a long swim. Visit a local beach café and try a traditional Greek breakfast of dakos (barley rusk with tomato and feta) — a Cretan specialty found across Greece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shopping afternoon in the local town — browse boutiques for handmade jewelry, linen clothing, natural cosmetics with Greek herbs (olive oil soap, thyme honey cream), and local spirits like mastiha or tsipouro to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Book a sunset boat cruise if available — many resorts offer 2-3 hour evening cruises with wine and light snacks as the sun sets over the sea (~€35-55 per person). A magical way to spend a Greek evening.

meals.breakfast: Dakos with Greek coffee at a local café — simple, fresh, and delicious (~€7-10)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in town — moussaka, a Greek salad, and sparkling water (~€14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Light dinner on the sunset boat cruise with wine and mezze, or a simple dinner back at the resort (~€20-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Budget €50-100 for souvenirs and shopping. Bargaining is not typical in shops but is acceptable at open-air markets. Natural Greek products like olive oil, saffron, and mountain tea make excellent gifts and are TSA/customs-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — swim, snorkel, and soak in the Aegean one last time. Take photos and enjoy the moment. Rent a paddleboat for a fun final morning on the water (~€10-15/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit any remaining sights on your list — a church, a viewpoint, or a neighborhood you haven't yet explored. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs. Pack non-essential items in the afternoon to ease tomorrow's departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant you've discovered during your trip. Celebrate the journey with a special meal and a bottle of Greek wine.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — make the most of the buffet spread (~€12-16)
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch — fresh calamari, Greek salad, and cold beer (~€14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant — a celebratory spread of your best-loved Greek dishes with a dessert of loukoumades or baklava and a complimentary shot of raki (~€28-38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ask the hotel to prepare a packed breakfast or early coffee for the next morning if your departure is early. Confirm transfer/taxi booking to the airport for Day 13. Settle any outstanding hotel bills in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — wake up for one last sunrise walk on the beach or a quiet coffee on the hotel terrace. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Transfer to the airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure — allow 2-3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse the airport duty-free for any last Greek purchases — olive oil, wine, or mastiha products.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories, a sun-kissed glow, and a collection of flavors, sights, and experiences to last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel or airport café — Greek pastry, fruit, and coffee (~€7-10)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or packed snacks for the flight
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep important documents (passport, boarding pass, travel insurance) easily accessible. Declare any food items (honey, cured meats) at customs if required. Greek airports can be busy in peak summer — arrive early. Kalo taxidi — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome drink and a leisurely check-in. Take a gentle stroll along the beachfront to orient yourself with the resort surroundings and settle into your luxurious beachfront suite.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on your private terrace watching the sunset over the Aegean Sea. Enjoy a light welcome cocktail at the resort's infinity pool bar before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Light mezze platter and fresh juice at the resort's beachfront lounge upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant – fresh catch of the day, grilled octopus, and local Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if possible. Unpack, rest, and hydrate – the heat can be tiring after a long flight. Confirm all upcoming private excursions with the resort concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a lavish breakfast at the resort's sea-view terrace restaurant. Afterwards, spend the morning at the resort's private beach – swim in the warm Aegean waters, relax on a sun lounger with complimentary chilled towels, and enjoy the crystal-clear sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion along the local coastline. Explore hidden sea caves, snorkel in secluded turquoise coves, and anchor at a pristine private beach accessible only by water. The boat includes a chilled champagne and fresh fruit spread.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a cliffside bar near the resort with panoramic Aegean views. Dress smart-casual for a memorable evening.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet at the resort's terrace restaurant – Greek yogurt with thyme honey, fresh pastries, eggs to order, smoked salmon, and seasonal fruits
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch served on the private boat – grilled prawns, Greek salad, crusty bread, and chilled local rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated local taverna near the resort – slow-roasted lamb kleftiko, spanakopita, and a bottle of aged Naoussa red wine

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen and bring a hat for the boat excursion. Book the private boat through the resort concierge in advance. Temperatures will reach 29°C – stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga session on the beach at sunrise, arranged through the resort. Follow with a refreshing swim in the calm morning sea before breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the nearest ancient archaeological site or historic village. Explore centuries-old ruins, Byzantine churches, and local architecture with a knowledgeable private guide who brings history to life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a rejuvenating spa treatment – opt for a traditional Greek olive oil massage or a sea-salt body scrub at the resort's luxury spa.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort – Greek frittata with feta and sun-dried tomatoes, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a cold-brew coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a charming local village taverna during the tour – moussaka, dakos (Cretan bruschetta), and a carafe of house wine
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining experience on your terrace – a curated 4-course Greek tasting menu with wine pairings arranged by the resort chef

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the archaeological site tour. The private guide can tailor the pace and depth of the tour to your preferences. Book the spa treatment at least one day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local fish market or morning food market with a private culinary guide. Discover fresh produce, local cheeses, cured meats, olives, and honey while learning about Greek food culture and regional specialties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Greek cooking class with a renowned local chef. Use the morning's market ingredients to prepare traditional dishes such as dolmades, fresh tzatziki, grilled sea bream, and loukoumades (honey doughnuts) for dessert.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely evening stroll along the waterfront promenade. Browse boutique shops for local ceramics, olive wood products, and artisan goods.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort – fresh fruit platter, Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, and herbal mountain tea
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class, paired with local wine selected by the chef
meals.dinner: Dinner at an acclaimed seafood restaurant on the waterfront – whole grilled sea bass, shrimp saganaki, and a bottle of crisp Chablis-style Greek white wine

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a highlight of the trip – request a vegetarian or dietary-specific menu adaptation if needed. The market is best visited before 10:00 AM for the freshest selection.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at the resort's private beach. Rent a kayak or stand-up paddleboard and explore the calm coastal waters at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to a nearby renowned beach known for its dramatic scenery – think crystal-clear water, white pebbles or golden sand, and striking rock formations. Spend the afternoon swimming and soaking up the sun in a premium beach club setting with reserved sunbeds and table service.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the beach club as the sun dips below the horizon. Watch the sky transform into shades of orange and pink over the sea.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet – pastries, cold cuts, cheeses, eggs Benedict, and fresh smoothies
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch – lobster linguine, grilled calamari, Greek salad with barrel-aged feta, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Return to the resort for dinner at the poolside grill – premium Wagyu beef souvlaki, grilled halloumi, roasted vegetables, and a bold Greek Xinomavro red wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transfer to the beach club through the resort. Arrive by 12:00 PM to secure the best sunbed positions. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the marine environment.

day_by_day.morning: Private sailing trip on a traditional wooden caïque boat. Sail along the coastline, stopping at two or three secluded bays for swimming and snorkeling. The boat crew will prepare fresh snacks on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the sailing journey to a picturesque fishing village. Disembark and wander through narrow whitewashed alleys, visit a local chapel, and browse artisan shops before sailing back.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant dinner at the resort's rooftop restaurant with sweeping sea views under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort – croissants, cold cuts, local honey, and espresso
meals.lunch: On-board caïque lunch – freshly caught fish grilled on deck, Greek salad, olives, bread, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine dining – seared scallops with saffron sauce, slow-braised lamb with orzo, and a premium Greek Moschofilero white wine

day_by_day.notes: The caïque sailing experience is weather-dependent – confirm with the crew the morning of. Bring a light layer for the boat as the sea breeze can be refreshing. Sunglasses and a hat are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation day. Begin with a long, indulgent breakfast on your private terrace. Then spend the morning at the resort's luxury spa – enjoy a couple's or solo thermal circuit, hot stone massage, and hydrotherapy pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lounge by the resort's infinity pool with a cocktail in hand. Order poolside snacks and enjoy the tranquility. Optionally, take a short nap in a shaded cabana.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset dinner on the beach, arranged exclusively by the resort – a table for two set directly on the sand with torchlight, a private waiter, and a personalized menu.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-suite breakfast – eggs royale, smoked salmon, Greek pastries, fresh fruit, and champagne
meals.lunch: Poolside light bites – mezze board with hummus, taramasalata, grilled pita, and a chilled glass of rosé
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner – lobster thermidor, truffle risotto, artisan cheese board, and a bottle of vintage Champagne

day_by_day.notes: This is your mid-trip rest day – fully embrace the luxury and slow pace. Book the private beach dinner experience at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. This is a perfect evening for a special occasion if applicable.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike along a scenic coastal trail near the resort. The path offers stunning views of the Aegean Sea and wildflower-dotted hillsides. A private guide can accompany you for safety and local insight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove and winery for a private tasting experience. Learn about the ancient tradition of Greek olive oil production and sample premium extra virgin olive oils alongside a curated selection of local wines.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a refreshing dip in the sea before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the hike – energy bars, fresh fruit, Greek yogurt, and coffee to go
meals.lunch: Winery lunch – artisan charcuterie, local cheeses, marinated olives, fresh bread, and paired wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at a celebrated local restaurant – grilled swordfish with capers and lemon, roasted eggplant with feta, and a bottle of Santorini Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy walking shoes for the coastal hike and carry 1.5 liters of water. The olive grove and winery visit typically lasts 2–3 hours. Confirm transportation with the concierge the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to a nearby island or peninsula by speedboat. Arrive early to enjoy the beaches before the crowds. Swim in impossibly clear water and explore the island's natural beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island's main village on foot or by golf cart rental. Visit local artisan workshops, a small museum, and enjoy the authentic atmosphere of a less-touristed Greek island.
day_by_day.evening: Speedboat return to the resort as the sun sets over the water – one of the most magical experiences of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before departure – eggs to order, pastries, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a family-run taverna on the island – fresh grilled fish of the day, village salad, and house-made lemonade
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort – grilled whole lobster, saffron-infused rice, and a premium Greek sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 09:00 AM to maximize time on the island. Bring cash as some smaller island establishments may not accept cards. The speedboat journey itself is exhilarating and scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided food tour of a nearby town or port. Visit a traditional bakery for fresh koulouri and tiropita, explore a spice shop, and stop at a local deli to sample cured meats and regional cheeses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local ceramics or artisan workshop and try a hands-on pottery class inspired by ancient Greek traditions. Take home a handmade piece as a unique souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a stylish rooftop bar in town before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast during the food tour – fresh-baked pastries, koulouri sesame bread, and Greek coffee at a local kafeneion
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Michelin-recognized or award-winning restaurant in town – creative modern Greek cuisine with local seasonal ingredients
meals.dinner: Back at the resort – a light dinner of mezze and grilled vegetables with a glass of chilled white wine on the terrace

day_by_day.notes: The food tour is best done on an empty stomach to fully enjoy all tastings. Wear comfortable shoes for walking on cobblestone streets. The pottery class is a fun, relaxed activity suitable for all skill levels.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the final full beach day at the resort's private beach. Swim, snorkel, and float in the warm Aegean Sea. Treat yourself to a beachside massage under a canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private yacht charter for the afternoon – sail to a stunning offshore sandbar or sea arch, anchor, and swim in the open sea. Champagne and canapés are served on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and dress for a special farewell-eve dinner at the resort's most exclusive dining venue.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast – full buffet with made-to-order omelets, smoked fish, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Yacht canapés and light bites – smoked salmon blinis, shrimp cocktail, and a bottle of Moët & Chandon Rosé
meals.dinner: Gala dinner at the resort's premium restaurant – 6-course tasting menu featuring the best of Greek land and sea, with wine pairings curated by the resort sommelier

day_by_day.notes: This is a day to truly indulge and savor the luxury experience before the trip winds down. Tip the yacht crew and resort staff generously for exceptional service throughout your stay.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning swim in the Aegean Sea at sunrise. Pack any remaining items and prepare for checkout. Enjoy one last breakfast at the resort's sea-view terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely checkout from Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on departure time, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a local café in the nearest town, or browse last-minute souvenirs – high-quality olive oil, local honey, saffron, and handmade jewelry make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to the airport or port for onward journey. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day Greek luxury experience.

meals.breakfast: Final grand resort breakfast – the full spread, enjoyed slowly with a glass of fresh orange juice and Greek mountain tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café – a classic Greek salad, fresh pita with hummus, and a cold frappe coffee
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport lounge or on the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and private transfer arrangements the evening before. Allow extra time at the airport for security. Carry any olive oils or liquids in checked luggage to comply with airline regulations.

day_by_day.morning: If the itinerary includes a buffer day before the return flight, use this morning for any last-minute exploration – a final swim, a visit to a local museum, or simply a long coffee at a harborside café watching fishing boats come in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: Visit a high-end local spa in town for a final indulgent treatment – a hammam experience or aromatherapy facial to arrive home feeling completely refreshed.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Greece – enjoy a memorable dinner at a top-rated waterfront restaurant, toasting to the journey with a glass of ouzo and fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery – fresh spanakopita, bougatsa (custard pastry), and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at a harbor taverna – grilled octopus, tzatziki, dolmades, and a cold Mythos beer
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a top waterfront restaurant – whole grilled sea bream, lobster pasta, and a final bottle of premium Santorini Assyrtiko under the stars

day_by_day.notes: This buffer day ensures no rushing and allows flexibility for flight delays or last-minute experiences. Use it to decompress, shop, or simply sit by the sea and absorb the beauty of Greece one last time. Kalό taxídi – safe travels!
